newsitem.title: USA: Craig Consumer files for Chapter 11.
newsitem.headline: Craig Consumer files for Chapter 11.

text.p: Craig Consumer Electronics Inc on Friday said it iled a Chapter 11 bankruptcy petition in order to reorganize its finances.
The case was filed in the Central District of California in Los Angeles.
Craig said the filing was prompted by a sales decline, excessive returns, particular difficulties in obtaining product from the company's Chinese joint venture, and slower-than-usual collections.
Those factors all detracted its borrowing capacity and cash flow, limiting its access to capital, it said.
Craig sells audio electronic products through retail chains, mass merchandisers, catalogs and direct-marketing companies.

"The borrowing limits and cash flow difficulties over the recent period have virtually eliminated access to capital for operating expenses and meaningful inventory supplies," the company said in a statement.
In connection with the Chapter 11 filing, Craig Consumer said it was entering into financing arrangements, all of which must be approved by the bankruptcy court.

The arrangements include debtor-in-possession advances from BT Commercial Corp, as agent for a syndicate of lenders. The advance will enable the company to ship products and actively conduct its business pending the proposal of a definitive plan of reorganization, it said.

The company said it expected to fill all existing customer orders for the sale of products to its creditworthy customers. In addition, it said it hoped ongoing sales, together with the financing and supply arrangements entered into with one of its principal vendors, will enable reorganization of "a more healthy, if not smaller, Craig."

"These have been difficult times in our industry and the confluence of circumstances that weakened our capacity for financing can hopefully be overcome," Chief Executive Richard Berger said in a statement. "We are hopeful that we can build enterprise value through the reorganization process, assuming the continued support of our senior lenders and principal vendors."
